# s268 — Offer the example relay roles matrix from slicer init

`slicer init` sets up a project but never mentions the relay roles matrix, so a new project finds `slicer relay-roles init` only once it runs `ai relay`. This slice adds an opt-in `init --relay-roles` that writes the example matrix along with the rest of `.slicer/`. Without the flag, `init` prints a one-line hint naming `slicer relay-roles init`.

**Findings:** owner, 2026-10-14: a new project should get the example matrix or be told about it at init; chose opt-in init --relay-roles plus a hint · **Size:** S · **Tree:** slicer

**2026-10-14** — Ready for review: init --relay-roles writes and renders the example matrix via ops.roles_init under the project lock and keeps an existing one; plain init prints the relay-roles hint only while no matrix exists, and a directory at the matrix path exits io. 7 new tests; full suite 1915 OK (skipped 1); gate PASS.

trust: unverified; by: Jon Robbins

**Not in this slice:**

## Why

The owner asked on 2026-10-14 for a default matrix to come with a new project, or at least be suggested when the project is first set up. Installing cannot do it, because `pip install` runs before any project exists, so `init` is the place. The owner chose an opt-in flag plus a hint, not writing it by default: projects that never run a relay should not carry an unused file, and every new project still learns that the matrix exists.

## Files

- `src/slicer/cli.py`: the `--relay-roles` flag on `init` and its help text. In `cmd_init`, the write after `ops.init_project`, rendering the matrix as `relay-roles init --render` does, plus the hint line.
- `src/slicer/ops.py`: only if `cmd_init` needs a small helper to load the new state and call `roles_init` under the project lock. Mutations stay in `ops.py`.
- `tests/test_cli.py` (the `test_Init_*` tests).
- `docs/commands.md` (the `init` row), `docs/agents.md` (the `init` JSON row), `docs/getting-started.md` (where the relay roles matrix is introduced), `CHANGELOG.md` `[Unreleased]`.

## Failing tests

- `test_Init_RelayRolesFlag_WritesExampleMatrixAndRender`: `init --relay-roles` leaves `.slicer/relay-roles.json` equal to what `relay-roles init` writes in a second fresh project. `relay-roles show` succeeds, and `check` passes with the render current.
- `test_Init_NoRelayRolesFlag_PrintsHintAndWritesNoMatrix`: plain `init` writes no matrix and prints a line naming `slicer relay-roles init`.
- `test_Init_Json_PayloadUnchangedWithoutFlag`: the `--json` payload of plain `init` is still exactly `{root, dir}`. With `--relay-roles` it adds `relay_roles: PATH`.
- `test_Init_ForceRelayRolesExistingMatrix_KeepsIt`: after a `relay-roles add`, `init --force --relay-roles` exits 0, leaves the matrix byte for byte, and says it was kept.
- `test_Init_RelayRolesFlag_NoHintLine`: with the flag, the hint line is not printed.

## Implement

1. Add the flag and help text: "also write the example relay roles matrix (see `relay-roles init`)".
2. In `cmd_init`, after `init_project`, when the flag is set and no matrix exists, write it through `ops.roles_init` and render it. When one exists, report that it was kept.
3. Without the flag, append the hint line before the git setup hint when no matrix exists.
4. Update the docs and the CHANGELOG. Mutation-check each new assertion.

## Check

- The full suite passes on Python 3.11+.
- In a scratch directory, `slicer init` with the new relay roles flag, then `slicer relay-roles recommend` on a new item, works, and `slicer check` passes. Plain `slicer init` prints the hint.
- `slicer check` and `git diff --check` pass.

## Git

Worktree `.worktrees/s268`, branch `feature/s268-init-relay-roles`. Commit only on the branch. Merging and pushing wait for the owner.

## Boundary

- `init` writes nothing new without `--relay-roles`. The hint is human output only, and the `--json` payload stays `{root, dir}` when no matrix is written.
- `--relay-roles` never replaces an existing matrix. `init --force --relay-roles` on a project that already has `.slicer/relay-roles.json` keeps it, says so, and still succeeds. Replacing a matrix stays with `relay-roles init --force`.
- The matrix written is exactly the one `relay-roles init` writes, through `ops.roles_init`, with no second copy of the example.
